refPrompt:
Use your image generation tool to create ONE pixel-art picture of the boss's office (CEO room) on the top floor of an office building, in EXACTLY the same pixel-art style, palette feel, dark outlines, pixel size, isometric camera angle, room shape (the same six-sided floor outline: wide back edge, slanted left and right wing walls, short front edge), same 2:1 aspect ratio (1024x512 look) and the same flat dark green background outside the room as the attached studio2.png. Do not draw any people. Do not use real brand names or readable text.
The room is a luxurious but cosy executive office: dark walnut floor boards, a big dark-red patterned rug in the middle, warm cream walls with dark wood wainscoting. The back wall and the left wall have tall large windows showing a HIGH-FLOOR city view (we are very high up: rooftops and skyscrapers far below, blue sky). On the RIGHT wall there is a big wooden-framed black chalkboard (dark green-black slate surface with a thick light-oak frame, empty, no writing, facing the room), and the door (dark wood, with a door frame) is also on the RIGHT wall near the front end, like the door in studio2.png.
Furniture: in the middle of the room, toward the back, one very big dark wooden executive desk in the same diagonal-free straight orientation as the lead desk of studio2 (long side parallel to the back wall) with a computer monitor on it seen from the BACK (the monitor back faces the viewer, absolutely no screen picture visible), a desk lamp, a few papers, and behind the desk (far side) a BIG tall-backed brown leather executive chair. In front of the desk (viewer side) lots of free floor for visitors. A cream-leather guest sofa with a low coffee table on the left side, a tall wooden bookcase full of books flush against the back wall, a trophy display cabinet with glass doors and golden trophies against the left wall, a big leafy plant in a pot near the right wall, and a wooden coat stand next to the door. Wall-mounted lamps and a couple of framed pictures on the walls.
Render crisp pixel art, no anti-aliasing blur, no text, no watermark. Save the result as ceo.png in the current directory.

views.dayPrompt: Wide panorama of a sunny big city seen from the TOP FLOOR of a very tall skyscraper (we are higher than almost everything): pale blue sky with a few small white clouds in the upper part, a hazy skyline of distant small blue-grey towers sitting on the horizon (haze fades them toward the sky colour), and below the horizon the view looks DOWN over the city: many mid-height beige, pink and blue-grey building roofs with tiny roof details, thin streets with tiny cars as dots, a pale river curving through, and a few green park patches. Strong scale difference: far towers very small, nearer roofs medium, the nearest roofs along the bottom edge larger. Only one or two taller towers rise to a similar height as the viewer. Pixel art, 16-bit era, same rendering style, palette and pixel size as the attached style reference (it is a crop of the old window view of this room: match colours and brush, ignore its composition). Flat 2-3 tone shading, about 48 colours, soft low contrast for far things. One single continuous wide landscape, NOT several separate pictures. No window frame, no glass, no reflection, no text, no people, no characters, no border, no vignette. Output exactly the aspect ratio of the attached guide image; the horizon is the thin red line of the guide image (do not draw the red line), keep the horizon on that line across the whole width. The attached images in order: style reference, aspect/horizon guide. Save the final image as view-day.png in the current directory.
views.nightPrompt: Edit the attached day image into a night version of EXACTLY the same picture: every building, street, river, bridge, park and the skyline stay in exactly the same pixel positions and shapes, the horizon stays on the same row, nothing moves, nothing is added or removed in the landscape. note: reference art/floors/ceo.png = ceo-ref2 (second Codex call: edit of the first reference) resized to 1024x512. Raw Codex output, sheets and pieces live outside the repo (AGENT_OFFICE_ART_WORK/ceo). The raw 8-pane window quads were measured from the shell (glass.json ceo). scene.json is the source of truth for footprints, seats and points. Pieces: piece-0 (desk) had its monitor and stand repainted to a neutral dark grey (saturation <= 0.25, nightmap monitorRule) before atlas.py. Sky masks: art/skymask.py has no ceo row; the same script run with ROOMS['ceo'] = dict(dist=12, hole=8000, bright=None) wrote sky-day.png and sky-night.png (night boundary step x3.17). Outline: art/backdrop.py simplification with --eps=2.5 (12 points), written into scene.json by hand because the regex of backdrop.py only matches a one-line outline. art/scene_sheet.py indexes seats[5] and stops on a room without seats, so the check sheet was made with a copy that uses the lead desk.
